subject.title: fix(update): prevent compatible plugins from being skipped after npm-global upgrades

question: Is the disclosed split Windows lifecycle using synthesized production JavaScript sufficient proof for this narrow update-handoff fix, or is one uninterrupted update and restart using an artifact built from the exact PR head required?
rationale: Source, focused tests, and production-backed output support the implementation; the remaining choice is the repository's proof threshold rather than a mechanical code defect.

options.title: Accept disclosed proof
options.body: Treat the real package replacement, compatible-plugin convergence, restart recovery, authenticated health, and enabled discovery as sufficient despite the split lifecycle and synthesized artifact.

options.title: Require exact-head lifecycle
options.body: Hold merge until one managed npm-global update completes replacement, convergence, restart, health, and discovery using an artifact built from the exact PR head.

recommendation.title: Accept disclosed proof
recommendation.body: Treat the real package replacement, compatible-plugin convergence, restart recovery, authenticated health, and enabled discovery as sufficient despite the split lifecycle and synthesized artifact.

likelyOwner.reason: They approved and merged the closest predecessor compatibility fix and are the strongest history-backed owner for this proof-threshold decision.
